**WORTH READING***
This has been one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had. When I arrived, the room looked dirty, and aside from the bed being made, it clearly wasn’t properly cleaned. On top of that, the night manager mistakenly charged my card over $400 for parking, despite the fact that I was already paying $370+ for the room. He claimed he immediately refunded the money, but when I checked out, I was told no refund had actually been processed until the GM handled it later.

I spent almost two weeks going back and forth with the staff. First, they refunded just $30, then told me they would only return $336 because of that initial refund—forcing me to send receipts, screenshots, and proof that they were consistently giving me wrong information. In the end, they still never refunded the full amount, and I had to go through my bank to get my money back, which took another 30 days.

Now, four months later, the hotel randomly charged my account $375 again—even though I’m nowhere near Miami and have not stayed there since. This is completely unacceptable. Not only do they make repeated billing errors, but they also offer no compensation, no apology, and no sense of responsibility for the stress and inconvenience they cause. They act as if simply issuing refunds—months later—is good enough.

This hotel should honestly be taken over by a company that knows how to run a property correctly and maintain proper billing practices. No one should have to deal with money being taken out of their account at random, especially during the holiday season.

text.text:
We had a very nice stay here but there were a few things worth noting that we did not like.
The hotel is currently undergoing renovations, starting with the penthouse floor and we were right below that so we heard quite a bit of the construction. The service elevator was clearly not working since the construction workers were using the guest elevators, of which there were only 2. This made for long wait times for the elevators.
Our room was ready for us immediately upon check in (earlier than normal check in time), which was amazing! And while it was spotlessly clean and had a stunning ocean view, there were noticeable holes in the curtains and shower curtain. There were many signs of wear/tear all over the hotel, making it clear why the renovation was needed.
The pool was NOT heated and this made a huge difference. Despite the 80 degree weather and warm (strong) winds, the water was too cold for me to go in and my kids even took a long time getting used to the water.
The beach staff were very nice and even came over to where the kids were digging in the sand to place an umbrella over them. There were also sand toys for them to play with.
The staff were exceptional. Front desk people were friendly, the cafe staff were amazing, and housekeeping did an amazing job keeping our room clean.
Would recommend this hotel for anyone on a budget.

Extremely disappointing stay.

Check-in set the tone: the front desk didn’t greet me at all—when I walked up, the employee just said “ID.” No welcome, no smile. I also booked a standard room with one bed but was going to be put in a room with two small beds instead. I’m a Platinum Elite member and received no acknowledgment of status and no welcome gift.

The room itself was unacceptable. There was toilet paper with pubic hair on it in the toilet, hair on the towels, and what looked like blood or nail polish on the bathtub. The room phone’s service buttons didn’t work at all.  The key cards repeatedly failed—they had to be reprogrammed at check-in and then again the next day because they stopped working before checkout.  The view was of rooftop mechanical equipment that made constant noise day and night.

The property is also poorly maintained. Peeling paint, a peeling office chair in the room, and in the fitness room, the treadmill belt seam was separating, which is honestly a huge safety hazard.

Between the rude service, cleanliness issues, and maintenance problems, this stay fell far below what I expect from a Holiday Inn. Management should seriously address these issues.

This place does not deserve to call itself a hotel. Poor service, hidden fees, rude staff, and no basic amenities.
Worst Miami stay experience ever.
I will never come back and strongly suggest others avoid this place too.

text.text:
This review is for anyone who is vacationing here with the intentions of driving - meaning you rented a car and plan to travel by driving yourself.

I do not recommend this place as a place to do so. In fact - if you are driving I don’t recommend staying in Miami period.

It’s incredibly not-driver-friendly. The parking spots here are incredibly limited and extremely hard to park into. Unless you are renting a truck or a high-clearance vehicle, you will struggle. The way the parking spaces are located you will have to jump the curb. No way around that.

We stayed in room 208. The toilet does not flush. There was an unlined rubbish bin that we used to fill up with water to manually flush the toilets. The shower had little pressure. Anyone with long or lots of hair will find themselves showering for a long time.

If you are on foot however and you don’t mind the subpar room amenities - I actually think this place isn’t that bad. Just remember you will need to depend on either ride shares or the public transportation to get to anywhere.

I do wish that the property management company invest in upgrading their room card readers. The cards they use are extremely out of date and are extremely sensitive to data corruption. The receptionist who checked us in kept repeating herself to emphasize that the card cannot be near smart phones or wallet. Anything NFC or RFID capable will corrupt the card and you will be locked out of your room. Happened to us and other residents.

They do however have 24/7 front desk service so I guess it’s not that bad.

I accidentally booked two weeks later than intended and immediately called the third party agent to ask for the 7 nights booking to be cancelled and I would rebook the correct dates (the online reservation calendar jumps to a date 2 weeks forward and highlights that day which misleads a distracted mind). They contacted the hotel who refused the request and would not transfer or allow a refund of any amount for cancellation. I decided to book another night and headed to the hotel to check in and try to negotiate a fair outcome. The receptionist reiterated the hotel policy which of course is not fair or necessary just because you have written acquisitive terms and greedy conditions into a policy.  So we stayed the night and turned out we would have abandoned our reservation anyway given the disgusting state of the property. The room and furnishings were filthy and of very poor quality. The walls are paper thin and the property sits on a main road so you are disturbed by noise from inside and outside the building. The ceiling fan was misaligned and also making lots of noise so had to be turned off. We dressed in track suits to minimize contact with the bed sheets which smelled like body odor and triggered formication or possibly we were actually being bitten by bed bugs. The WIFI is so slow as to be unusable and the staff were combative when we requested it be remedied.
It really is a two star hotel at best and the 2.5 stars they had needs to be amended.

If you’re looking for a sophisticated yet approachable escape in the heart of Mid-Beach, Le Particulier Miami is a hidden gem that absolutely nails the "modern Miami" aesthetic. I recently stopped by to try their cafe, and the experience was top-tier from the moment I walked through the door.
Modern Design Meets Art Deco Soul
The first thing you notice is the atmosphere. The design is very nice and modern, successfully blending 1980s glamour with a minimalist Art Deco twist. The space feels incredibly chic, with a palette of soft pastels, warm oak, and brass accents that make it feel more like a private sanctuary than a standard hotel lobby. It’s the kind of place where you actually want to linger and soak in the "lobby oasis" vibe rather than just grabbing your drink and rushing out.
The Perfect Americano
I’m quite particular about my coffee, but the Americano here was great. It was well-balanced, smooth, and served at the perfect temperature—not bitter at all, which is a common pitfall. Whether you’re a local needing a quiet place to work for an hour or a traveler looking for a high-quality caffeine fix, their cafe service is efficient and the quality is undeniable.
Final Thoughts
The location on Collins Avenue is ideal—tucked away from the chaotic noise of South Beach but still vibrant and accessible. The staff were friendly and unhurried, which really adds to the "lifestyle" feel of the property. Between the stunning interior design and the excellent coffee, it’s a spot I’ll definitely be returning to. It’s a perfect example of how a modern boutique hotel should handle its food and beverage experience.

Positives:  Big open room. Large refrigerator with ice maker (water dispenser broken unfortunately).  Front desk answers the phone most of the time (but they do not call you back if you leave a message).  They went from 2 to 3 stars for printing our cruise luggage tags for us.

Negatives: lots of single paned windows with cheap 1” miniblinds that do not block light or dampen sound. Curtains really aren’t that expensive and if you got thick curtains, it would block out the ridiculous amount of honking and noise. It would also keep me from being awakened in an incredibly bright room as soon as the sun comes up.  This may not be as problematic on rear facing rooms, but we were third floor facing street, Very loud.

Don’t believe that you’ll be able to watch TV in the room. I know you don’t come to Miami to watch TV, but at some point it’s nice to be able to turn on the TV and wind down, or in my case I wanted some background noise to block out the ridiculous outside noise . They should fire DIRECTV and get with the new times. The Wi-Fi is decent after I asked them to reset the modem because it wasn’t working very well. Network TV and streaming would fix a lot of problems, but the satellite pixelates every five seconds.  The worker came up and just said what’s the problem, that is what satellite does. Um, no, not on a clear night.

Please put some coffee in the room when there is a coffee maker already there. It’s not expensive and it’s a great luxury after a terrible night of sleep.

For me ultimately the value of a hotel is ability to relax and get a good night sleep.  We were planning to come back after the cruise, but they failed at this, so I cancelled the room for next week.

text.text: We stayed here with 2 adult kids and our 5 year old grandson for 5 nights because the hotel is located not far from relatives.  Although the suite was clean and had plenty of space we found the hotel to be inhospitable and the front desk to be unfriendly.  Although we had booked for 5 people when we arrived only 2 beds were made up and there were insufficient sheets and towels and when we asked for more  we were told they would be sent up but that did not happen until we went back again hours later.  When a pipe burst in our room the staff did come up to stop the leak and mop the room as soon as we called them, and they did quickly offer a replacement room but left us to drag our own bags and possessions through the floodwater and upstairs to the new room without offering to assist as our grandson cried. And then we once again had to pull out and make 3 of the beds in the new room- no assistance from hotel staff.  This ruined what was meant to be a relaxing afternoon but when we asked for a courtesy discount or accommodation at checkout the person at the front desk who identified himself as the owner declined and seemed to think the hotel should get an award for supplying a replacement room.  Personally I think we are fortunate they had a replacement room available because the feeling we were left with is that if they did not they would have just told us to checkout or offered us to stay in the flooded room without any discount. On Friday night when we returned to the hotel from dinner we were met by a panicked non-English speaking hotel guest who identified himself to us in Yiddish and Hebrew as a fellow Sabbath observer who was locked out of his room and asked us for help communicating the issue with the front desk. The attendant at the front desk indicated he knew the man was a hotel guest and was amenable to providing the gentleman with a new keycard but refused to cooperate at all to open his door for him. I assisted the man in communicating with another friendly hotel guest who genially agreed to come up and open his room door. While I do not expect Sabbath accommodation from every hotel we stay in (and we in fact left our door open to avoid bothering them), I do feel that in the circumstances where a guest of the hotel needed the simple courtesy of assistance in opening his door a decent and hospitable hotel would spend the 3 minutes to assist him as we have found to be the case in numerous other hotels both nationally and internationally. But in this case the desk attendant informed us that is was “not his problem” and suggested that this man find another guest to assist him (which as mentioned we were able to do because unlike the hotel attendant, the other guests wanted to be helpful). In any event if you are looking for hospitality in Miami Beach there are plenty of other hotels, and I’d recommend finding a different one.

I ended my membership after many years because the overall experience has become unacceptable.

Service quality is consistently poor. Staff members often appear unmotivated, insufficiently trained, and in some cases openly unfriendly. Simple requests turn into drawn-out processes, food service takes an unreasonable amount of time, and the end result rarely justifies the wait.

The beach area is almost permanently overcrowded and poorly managed. Instead of feeling exclusive or relaxing, it feels hectic and neglected. Several areas of the property are visibly worn down, poorly maintained, and at times simply unpleasant to use. This is not an environment where you feel comfortable spending time.

What ultimately led to my decision was the general lack of respect shown toward members. Rules are enforced in an unnecessarily confrontational way, without empathy or basic judgment. Rather than feeling welcomed, you are made to feel like a problem.

Avoid becoming a member.

I'm writing this review as a warning to those who are considering renting a suite at the Residences via Airbnb and NOT through the hotel.  The Private Residences management company based in NYC that manages units in this building via Airbnb essentially STOLE $2,807.54 from me.  I'm shocked and alarmed at how little protection the paying customer has in the arrangement.   Airbnb is essentially indifferent to the theft.  And Fontainebleau management themselves has very little authority in the situation.

Had I known we had so little protection as a paying customer I never would have gone through Airbnb.

My wife and her girlfriends rented a two bedroom suite for 3 nights at the Residences via airbnb for a weekend getaway.  It was our first time using the service and it seemed like a good deal.  On Friday October 11th they checked into the room and found it to be dirty and in disrepair.  Attached are photos.  The deal-breaker issues were mold on the fridge and shower (one guest had allergies) and the poorly patched fist-sized holes in the walls (another guest was a survivor of domestic violence) There were also stains on the curtains, splatters on the walls around the toilet, scattered sticky spots, hair and clothing tags on the floor, etc.  Very grimy vibe.  They felt extremely uncomfortable and immediately notified airbnb and the front desk at the hotel.  The Host did offer another room to stay in, but they were exhausted & disheartened with the airbnb experience so they opted to cancel the room and purchase 2 new rooms directly from the Fontainebleau hotel.  And then things got sketchy.

The Host refused to check them out of the suite or let them cancel the reservation, and then went dark. The next day, the Host texted novels of excuses and accusations, how unreasonable they were being for not wanting to stay in the Suite.  The case was escalated within airbnb, but the Host was unresponsive.  Finally on Sunday my wife sat down with a manager at Fontainebleau owner services who was very kind, and she checked them out of the suite.  The manager said there was nothing else the Hotel could do,  but we did get a printout from housekeeping documenting that the room was never used.

When the trip ended on Monday, October 14th we followed up on the case with airbnb and were told that.......
1. You can't get a full refund because you never checked out of the room.
2. The Host doesn't have to check you out early if they don't want to, even if you ask them to do it.  The Host also doesn't have to answer you if they don't feel like it.
3. The maximum refund you can get is 10% for the cleaning fee and a $300 courtesy credit.
4. It's at the Host's discretion if you get a refund or not.  If the Host says no, Airbnb is powerless to do anything.  Airbnb takes no responsibility and won't cover your loses.
5.  Even though airbnb acknowledges the room was dirty and in disrepair, it wasn't dirty ENOUGH to qualify for any further action.

The first airbnb rep I spoke with issued an ultimatum, that if I didn't take the partial credit by the end of her shift she was logging out of her terminal and closing our case, and I would get nothing.

Finally after 3 weeks of back-and-forth with airbnb we were able to get a little under $1,000 back, but still lost over $1,800 for a suite no-one stayed in.  I've never had so much taken from me in exchange for nothing.   Please think twice before using airbnb (or any 3rd party site for that matter) when booking your vacation.  You have no protection as a consumer.  And if you don't like what you're being given they will just keep your money anyway.

My stay at **Andaz Miami Beach** was nothing short of exceptional — a true 5-star property delivering a 5-star experience from start to finish.

I arrived looking for refuge from a snowstorm, and the property manager could not have been more gracious. He kindly upgraded my room, which was such a thoughtful gesture, and even sent a personal note along with a delicious treat waiting for me. That level of care and attention immediately made me feel welcomed and valued.

The room was absolutely beautiful — elegant, comfortable, and immaculately maintained. The pools were stunning and perfectly heated, making it easy to relax and unwind. While there are no hot tubs (which makes sense for Florida’s climate), one would certainly be a nice addition during the cooler winter months. The beach experience was just as lovely, and having two chairs and umbrellas included in the resort fee made it effortless to enjoy the oceanfront setting.

Although I didn’t have the opportunity to dine at the main restaurant, the poolside restaurant was delicious. We tried the burgers, salad, and salmon — all fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. It was the perfect complement to a relaxing day by the pool.

Another major plus: when paying fully with points, there were no additional fees — a rare and much-appreciated benefit that adds incredible value.

From the warm, personalized service to the beautiful accommodations and amenities, everything exceeded expectations. I would absolutely return — a flawless escape when I needed it most. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We booked a room at the Hotel Continental because of its proximity to the beach and its affordability compared to most of the Hilton properties south of 40th Street in Miami Beach.  We knew what we were in for in terms of amenities and room size, but were not at all disappointed.  The room was clean and the king mattress was great and we slept better here than in any Hampton Inn, HGI, etc which have huge welts in their mattresses.  Even the AC was smooth and calming. Leo checked us in and was very personable during our stay.  He had a great attitude about him.  Katy was very sweet and conversational with my wife and me.  She served us during happy hours and the next mornings at breakfast.  We loved talking with her and appreciated her hustle.

We used the hotel-provided, free beach chairs and towels each day and parked them close to the water’s edge, in front of the encampments from the neighboring Cadillac and Andaz hotels.  Our needs were simple this vacation, but the Hotel Continental managed to exceed our expectations.

We stayed in the Sorrento Tower, and while the view and location are nice, the actual experience was extremely disappointing for the price.

The room felt worn out and poorly maintained. Lighting was dim, the space did not feel properly cleaned, and the furniture on the deck was damaged, with broken and neglected items left outside. The overall condition of the room did not match what you would expect at this price point.

Basic amenities were a problem throughout the stay. The fridge in our room did not work, and food stored inside went warm. The bathtub would not drain, and the jets turned on randomly in the middle of the night, which was unsettling. The in-room washer and dryer were unusable due to a cut power cord, something we only discovered on the last night after loading it with laundry. Front desk staff had even sent detergent earlier, so there was no indication the machine didn’t work.

For a supposedly premium room, the coffee maker was the same basic Keurig you’d find in a low-end two-star hotel, which summed up the overall lack of attention to quality.

Check-in was also a mess. We were not given the correct rooms initially, and it took over half an hour to get things sorted out. On top of that, staff were consistently rude and difficult to get clear information from, which made the entire stay more frustrating than it needed to be.

Sorrento Tower is significantly overpriced for the condition and level of service provided. There are much better options in the area for less money. We would not stay in Sorrento Tower again and would not recommend it.

We were initially very happy with our stay—the apartment was clean, well-furnished, and offered a stunning view. The check-in process was smooth, and the host communicated promptly and clearly. These were the highlights of our experience.

However, what ultimately ruined our trip and left us deeply disappointed was the building’s elevator situation, which was not disclosed by the host in any way prior to our booking. The elevators were barely functioning throughout our stay. We often had to wait 40–70 minutes just to catch one, and on several occasions, we had no choice but to take the stairs—even from the 34th floor.

The most alarming incident involved my 13-year-old son, who got trapped in an elevator on the 23rd floor along with four other people. There were no working emergency alarms and no phone signal. They remained stuck until the doors eventually opened on their own. My son was terrified and ran down the stairs in a panic.

My husband, who is elderly and has mobility limitations, was effectively stuck in the apartment for most of our stay because he simply could not use the stairs. This situation caused enormous stress, physical strain, and completely disrupted the plans we had for our trip.

To make things worse, we learned from others in the building that this elevator issue is long-standing and well known—yet the host never mentioned it in the listing or during our communications. We felt misled and uninformed about a major safety and accessibility concern. Even after reporting the issue early during our stay, no meaningful action or compensation was offered.

At checkout, we had to begin the process hours early, anticipating long elevator delays, and struggled to move our luggage and help my husband exit safely.

While the apartment itself has potential, the ongoing elevator crisis and lack of transparency from the host made this a deeply stressful and disappointing experience. I would strongly advise future guests to ask direct questions about the elevator functionality before booking, especially if traveling with elderly family members or young children.
